title: tier-2 shipped code: bundle entry search against BundleEntryLookup (0x141fd5820)

unreachableBranches.why: width-4 path, reached only when lo < last. At loop exit lo == hi, and the last bound update must have been hi = mid (an update to lo = mid + 1 would leave lo > hi), so guids[lo] >= target and the 'guid < target -> return 0' edge cannot execute from the function entry.
width-2 path, same lo < last invariant and proof as the width-4 site.
width-1 path, same lo < last invariant and proof as the width-4 site.

width-4 lo < 0 test after the loop. lo is an unsigned index that starts at 0 and only ever becomes mid + 1 with mid <= last <= 0x7ffffffe for a non-negative i32 count, so its signed value is never negative. Negative counts are outside the unit's contract (the client's count gate compares count * stride with 0 and then indexes with count - 1).
width-2 path, same non-negative-index proof as the width-4 site.
width-1 path, same non-negative-index proof as the width-4 site.

notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-tank/src/bundle.rs, built by cargo and called by crates/ow-tank/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the bundle_lookup entry. The ledger binds the verdict to bundle.rs + the probe source + the git revision.

Oracle is BundleEntryLookup at exe 0x141fd5820 (v2b 0x7ff7c6cf5820; the offline image keeps RVA == file offset). Signature: (directory*, u64 handle, u64 GUID); the directory pointer in RCX is never read, the handle is RDX and the GUID is R8. It returns a pointer in RAX, not an out-parameter, and has no frame or callees.

The handle is the client's tagged bundle request handle: handle == u64::MAX and (handle & ~0x3f) == 0 return 0; the object at handle & ~0x3f must have a +8 dword whose low six bits equal the handle's low six bits; object +0 is the payload pointer and a null pointer returns 0. The fixture builds that object in the arena's first 64 bytes and the payload immediately after it.

Return adapter: the client returns payload + offset, a pointer into its own address space. The fixture passes the payload's guest base (ARENA_BASE + 0x40) in the client's dead RCX slot and the probe returns guest_base + offset (or 0), so both sides compare the same guest u64. The probe's bundle_lookup discards the handle's address bits; it only carries the handle's tag to the shipped entry_lookup, which is the same check the client performs.

The search is crates/ow-tank/src/bundle.rs offset_of: bounds 0 and count - 1 (not a half-open [0, count)), midpoint (lo + hi) >> 1, lower bound then an exact GUID equality, then the width-byte offset. Offset 0 is the client's absent value. entry_lookup adds the client's handle guard, the width gate (a width other than 1, 2 or 4 returns 0 before any entry read) and the null payload pointer check.

The fixture is synthetic: widths 1/2/4 (and 0/3 to prove the width gate), counts 0/1/2/3/8, first/middle/last found rows, absent before/between/after, duplicate GUIDs (the lower bound is the first equal row, and a zero offset there is absent), unsorted tables that follow the client's walk rather than a linear scan, offset 0, GUID 0, u64::MAX, and tables whose last row ends at the payload's final byte. No install bytes and no offset into the install are used.

Unsorted behaviour is the reason the shipped search was changed: the old half-open [0, count) walk returns absent for [2, 1] looking for 2 while the client reads entry 0 and returns its offset. A bundle is GUID-sorted on the install, so the old code was exact on real data but not on the client's bytes.

The differential covers the client's handle guard, all three width paths, both post-loop shapes, the loop's repeat and exit, and the offset-0 test. The three 'lo < last and GUID < target' edges and the three 'lo < 0' edges are structurally dead and declared in unreachableBranches; every other branch is hit by both edges.
